summary: The 1982-83 TV series adapts the Weekly Shonen Jump serialisation of Cobra from installment 1 through the 「シドの女神」(Salamander) arc — i.e. chapters 1-76 of the 156-installment Jump run, Jump Comics volumes 1-8. ja.wikipedia states it directly (原作の連載第1話から「シドの女神」編までが描かれている) and en.wikipedia's episode list says 'loosely based in the first eight volumes'. CHAPTER SPACE: the entry's 156 chapters / 18 volumes is the original Jump Comics serialisation space and that is what these anchors use; MangaUpdates' latest_chapter=28 is a STORY count (the 28 discrete Cobra stories, matching fr.wikipedia's 'Histoires' list), not a chapter numbering — which is exactly open flag #676, and the reason the stored ep31 anchor reads 'chapter 14' (= story 14, 「シドの女神」). The adaptation is genuinely REORDERED, not linear: ja.wikipedia's character article says so twice in as many words (the Sword-people story was lifted out of the middle of the tattoo storyline and aired as eps 20-21 with its planet renamed Zados→Bakoosa; 「死の商人」編にあたる第25話 airs before 「二人の軍曹」 at ep26). Six blocks are out of running order. The 31 episodes nonetheless partition chapters 1-76 exactly once each with no gaps and no overlaps, which is the strongest single check available here.

anchors.note: ja.wikipedia states the TV series is drawn '原作の連載第1話から' — from serialized installment 1. ch1 「復活!コブラの巻」 (WSJ 1978 #45) is the Johnson / Trip-Movie / Vaiken opening that ep1 dramatises.

ep2's Vivi / Zygoba story is the 「サイコガンの秘密」 arc (ja.wikipedia character article: ビビ 「サイコガンの秘密」編で登場…姉と共にジゴバに誘拐され). That story is one of the two 1977 one-shots remade inside the weekly run; by the character article's own ordering it sits between 「黄金の男」 and 「雷電の惑星」, i.e. ch32 「サイコ・ガンは心で撃ての巻」 — the punchline being that a copied Psychogun is useless because it is fired by will. Pulled forward to episode 2. See flags: ch20 「見えざる敵」 is the runner-up candidate.
Bar on Tugsard, bounty hunter Jane Royal, Crystal Boy's Killer Section captures them = ch2 「イレズミの女の巻」 + ch3 「クリスタル・ボーイ登場の巻」.
Sid Penitentiary: Cobra deliberately arrested, escapes, rescues Catherine = ch4 「捕らわれたコブラ」 / ch5 「脱出!!」 / ch6 「救出作戦」.
The masked sniper remotely puppeted by Tarvage = ch7 「姿なき狙撃手【スナイパー】の巻」.
Cobra's counter-attack and the magician's identity = ch8 「コブラの大逆襲」 / ch9 「魔術師ターベージ」 (Tarvage named in both the episode synopsis and the chapter title).
Catherine's funeral, Cobra's rage, then the plant-man Tarvage duel = ch10 「コブラのいかり」 / ch11 「コブラ対植物人間」.
Break-out, spaceport battle, Crystal Boy cornered, final duel = ch12-15 (「コブラとびだす」「宇宙港の戦い」「ボーイを追いつめた!」「最後の戦い」). Closes the first Crystal Boy block.
Snow Gorillas / the third sister on Lourouge = ch16 「第三の女」 / ch17 「鉄の戒律」.
Ski escape then the tattoo composite revealing planet Zados = ch18 「雪上の大追跡」 / ch19 「イレズミの秘密」 — the episode title 「イレズミの秘密」 is character-identical to ch19's.

Zados pyramid, Sandra beats Cobra inside, the weapon is found = ch24 「サンドラふたたび」 / ch25 「最終兵器発見」. The manga reaches these AFTER the Sword-people chapters (ch20-23) which the TV series relocated to eps 20-21.
Ultimate Weapon transforms, golden-giant Sandra, Mars Ancient History vol.3 on the pyramid roof = ch26 「最終兵器の秘密」 / ch27 「進化を阻止せよ」. ch26 is the chapter Jump Comics vol.3 is named after.
Las Vegas Station casino, Hammer Volt Joe, the missing Venus gold ship = the 「黄金の男」 arc (ja.wikipedia character article describes exactly this cast), ch30 「カジノ・ステーション」 / ch31 「かけ・・・!」.
ja.wikipedia character article: ガルタン 「宇宙の大魔王」編で登場、TV版では14話で登場する. ch28 「大魔王ガルタン」 (title identical to the episode's) / ch29 「魔王を倒せ」. Aired AFTER ep13 although it precedes it in the manga.
ja.wikipedia character article: ベガ 「雷電の惑星」編で登場…TV版では15話で登場し、大幅な設定の追加がなされた. ch35 「雷電の惑星」 / ch36 「翼・・・!!」 (Vega's winged moult) / ch37 「コブラの帰還」. ch35 is the chapter JC vol.4 is named after.
Rug-Ball arc opens: Cobra goes undercover as Joe Gillian with the Red Saxons = ch41 「ラグ・ボール」 / ch42 「秘密指令は殺しの匂い」. Arc START anchor.
Team Z assembled, the murder-game framing = ch43 「殺人ゲーム」 / ch44 「プレイ・ザ・ゲーム」.
First half of the match, Geck killed, Cobra's home run = ch45 「ブロックくずし」 / ch46 「先取点は死をかけて!」 / ch47 「死神のウインク」.

Round two, the bribe, the drug shipment data, the sign-off note = ch48 「美女のキスは逆転の味」 / ch49 「ウイニングボール」 / ch50 「おき手紙は領収書!!」. Arc END anchor: ch50 is the last Rug-Ball installment (WSJ 1979 #45) before a seven-issue hiatus.

ja.wikipedia character article, Babel: TV版では20話と21話で登場。エピソード順が変更されたことに伴い、舞台となる惑星が「最終兵器」の眠る惑星ザドスから「バクーサ」という惑星に変更されている. ch20 「見えざる敵」 / ch21 「ソード人の秘密」. In the manga this sits INSIDE the tattoo storyline, before the Ultimate Weapon.
King Jeek freed, duel with Babel = ch22 「ソード王ジーク」 / ch23 「ソードの真の王」 (episode title 「二人のソード王」). Second half of the relocated Sword-people arc.
ja.wikipedia character article: ジンガロ 「地底の客」編で登場…ライフル星…孫のユーコをさらわれ — exactly ep22's plot. ch38 「モビルライダーの襲撃」 / ch39 「無敵のモグラ作戦」 / ch40 「地下基地爆破」. Held back to air after the Rug-Ball block.

Ironhead, the sunken Queen Carady, the undersea vault = ch55 「異常なる島」 / ch56 「アイアンヘッド登場」 / ch57 「妖女の殺し文句」 / ch58 「海底の墓標」. The episode title 「海底の墓標」 is character-identical to ch58's, which is also the chapter JC vol.6 is named after.
Episode title 「ロボットはいかが?」 is character-identical to ch33 「ロボットはいかが?の巻」; ch34 「反乱・・・!!」 is the robot uprising the episode ends on. Held back roughly ten episodes from its manga slot.
ja.wikipedia character article states plainly: 「死の商人」編にあたる第25話. Arms-dealer Brian Reed holds Lady hostage = ch53 「レディーを救え!!」 / ch54 「ジョイントをうて!!」.

ja.wikipedia character article: シエラ少尉 is 「二人の軍曹」編のヒロイン and the Royal Ruby split — ep26's Lieutenant Shella and the National Royal Rubies. ch51 「スパイはだれだ!?」 (she is the Domel spy) / ch52 「死の配当」 (the ruby cut). Aired AFTER ep25 although it precedes it in the manga.
Final arc 「シドの女神」 opens: Salamander appears, Dominique flayed, Lady bombed = ch59 「サラマンダー登場」 / ch60 「タートル号大爆発」 / ch61 「ダーティショット」. Arc START anchor (WSJ 1980 #10-#12).
Recruiting Fast-Fire Doug and springing Pumpkin = ch62 「0.1秒の男」 / ch63 「賞金首の仲」 / ch64 「鬼の笑う星」 / ch65 「トリックゲーム」.
Bud's polar laboratory = ch66 「バッド登場」 / ch67 「雪上の決戦」 / ch68 「クレージーショット」.
El Rodes raid, Doug's body-double infiltration of the Guild reunion = ch69 「かえ玉作戦」 / ch70 「血ぬられた出会い」 / ch71 「地獄のデス・マッチ」.

Finale. The team is killed, Miral Judd / the Elrado sect, the Shido Goddess launch = ch72 「友よやすらかに!」 / ch73 「熱い女は死の臭い」 / ch74 「死の宗教」 / ch75 「女神の秘密」 / ch76 「亡霊よ やすらかに」. ch76 (WSJ 1980 #29) is the last installment of Part 1: ja.wikipedia's 沿革 puts 第1部 at 連載開始〜「サラマンダー（シドの女神）」編 (1978-1980) and 第2部「黒竜王」編 at 1981, and the next installment ch77 is WSJ 1981 #2-3. en.wikipedia: 'Loosely based in the first eight volumes of the manga'; JC vol.8 is 「シドの女神の巻」.

continue_points.note: PARITY: ep11 resumes at ch24. ch20-23 (「ソード人の秘密」) are skipped here and animated later as eps 20-21, so a reader staying in step with the anime should leave them for then.
PARITY: ep13 resumes at ch30 (「黄金の男」). ch28-29 (「宇宙の大魔王」) are skipped here and animated next episode (ep14).
PARITY: ep15 resumes at ch35 (「雷電の惑星」). ch33-34 (「ロボットはいかが?」) are skipped here and animated at ep24.
PARITY: ep16 resumes at ch41 (Rug-Ball). ch38-40 (「地底の客」) are skipped here and animated at ep22.
Series end. Everything through ch76 (Jump Comics vol.8) has been animated; the reader continues at ch77, the first installment of Part 2 「黒竜王」 (WSJ 1981 #2-3), JC vol.9.

annotations.note: 「ソード人の秘密」 is embedded inside the tattoo/Ultimate-Weapon storyline in the manga; the TV series lifted it out and aired it as eps 20-21, after Rug-Ball, and moved the setting from Zados to a new planet 'Bakoosa' (ja.wikipedia character article, Babel entry). Dominique, who is present for it in the manga, is absent from the TV version for the same reason.
The 「サイコガンの秘密」 story (Vivi / Zygoba) sits at ch32 in the Jump run — it is one of the two 1977 one-shots remade inside the weekly serialisation — but was pulled all the way forward to episode 2.
Swapped pair: ep13 adapts 「黄金の男」 (ch30-31) and airs BEFORE ep14's 「宇宙の大魔王」 (ch28-29).
「ロボットはいかが?」 (ch33-34) held back roughly ten episodes, to ep24.
「地底の客」 (ch38-40) held back past the whole Rug-Ball block, to ep22.
Swapped pair: ep25 adapts 「死の商人」 (ch53-54) and airs BEFORE ep26's 「二人の軍曹」 (ch51-52).

ja.wikipedia records that the TV version applies 大幅な脚色 to characters and plot: Dominique is promoted from youngest to eldest sister, Vega gets an invented Wing-planet backstory and a six-hour lifespan (ep15), and ep25 adds an anime-original doctor character who revives the frozen Cobra (in the manga Lady simply drops him in a tank). Story skeletons still follow the manga.

repairs.why: The stored value is in MangaUpdates' STORY space (MU latest_chapter=28 = the 28 discrete Cobra stories; story 14 is 「シドの女神」/'La Deesse de Cid', which is indeed what ep31 finishes). The entry's chapter space is AniList's 156 chapters / 18 volumes = the Weekly Shonen Jump serialisation, in which the last installment of the 「シドの女神」 arc is ch76 (WSJ 1980 #29). volume=8 is CORRECT and should be left alone. Apply-script contract: this row is source='mu', so the repair must flip the row to source='manual' or the next MU re-derive will erase it.

structure.notes: One season, 31 broadcast episodes, our cumulative numbering == broadcast numbering; no OVAs/specials inside the range. CHAPTER SPACE: ja.wikipedia's manga infobox says 157話 while jajanken's issue-by-issue table of the Jump run and AniList both say 156 — a one-installment discrepancy somewhere in the 1981-84 stretch. Chapters 1-76 (our whole range) are a continuous, unambiguous run in the jajanken table, so the discrepancy does not move these anchors; a future anchor beyond ch~80 should re-check. VOLUMES: no source I could reach publishes the Jump Comics 18-volume chapter contents, so I have left volume null except where it is independently attested (ep1 -> v1; ep31 -> v8, per ja.wikipedia's JC volume list where v8 is 「シドの女神の巻」 and v9 「黒竜王の巻」 begins Part 2, plus en.wikipedia's 'first eight volumes'). A PROPOSED (derived, unverified) boundary set consistent with the volume titles, the ~9-11 month tankobon lag and an even ~9.5 chapters/volume is: v1 1-9, v2 10-19, v3 20-28, v4 29-38, v5 39-48, v6 49-58, v7 59-67, v8 68-76 — it puts each volume's title chapter inside that volume (v3 ch26 最終兵器の秘密, v4 ch35 雷電の惑星, v5 ch41 ラグ・ボール, v6 ch58 海底の墓標) and v7 「暗黒街の友」 over the Doug/Pumpkin/Bud recruitment stretch. Do NOT apply it without Sean's ruling. RELATED WORKS not in scope: the 1982 theatrical film コブラ SPACE ADVENTURE is a separate-continuity retelling of the tattoo-sisters story, and COBRA THE ANIMATION (2008 OVAs / 2010 TV) adapts LATER arcs (ザ・サイコガン, ギャラクシーナイツ, タイムドライブ and the 1982 mid-length stories) — none of those belong in this entry's episode space.

flags_for_sean: OPEN FLAG #676 ANSWERED: MU's latest_chapter=28 is not a chapter count — it is the count of discrete Cobra STORIES (fr.wikipedia lists exactly 28 'Histoires'). The reading edition / chapter space for this entry should be the Weekly Shonen Jump serialisation: 156 installments, Jump Comics 18 volumes, which is what AniList already stores. Recommend suppressing MU as a chapter-number source for this series.
REPAIR ep31 end_chapter 14 -> 76 (see repairs[]). The row is source='mu' and must be flipped to 'manual' on apply, per the hikaru lesson.

CONFIDENCE POSTURE: only eps 1 and 31 are 'high'. Every other anchor is 'medium' by construction — no source anywhere states a chapter NUMBER for any episode. What I have is (a) a complete, issue-by-issue Jump installment list with subtitles, (b) ja.wikipedia's character article giving explicit episode<->arc statements for eps 2, 13, 14, 15, 20, 21, 22, 25, 26, and (c) en.wikipedia's per-episode synopses. Cross-matching those three yields a partition of ch1-76 that covers all 31 episodes exactly once with no gaps or overlaps. That is strong, but it IS a derivation, not a citation of a number.

WEAKEST LINK: ep2. Its story (Vivi / Zygoba) is 「サイコガンの秘密」 per ja.wikipedia's character article, one of the two 1977 one-shots remade inside the weekly run, but no source places that remake at a specific installment. I put it at ch32 「サイコ・ガンは心で撃ての巻」 because (i) the character article orders 黄金の男 -> サイコガンの秘密 -> 雷電の惑星, which brackets it to ch32-34, (ii) ch33-34 are 「ロボットはいかが?/反乱」 (ep24, exact title match), leaving only ch32, and (iii) the story's punchline is that a duplicated Psychogun is useless because it fires by will — 'shoot the Psychogun with your heart'. Runner-up candidate is ch20 「見えざる敵」 (Zygoba phases through solids); if ch20 is ep2, then eps 20-21 shift to ch21-23 and ep13 takes ch30-32. Happy to drop ep2's anchor entirely if you would rather not carry it.

MINOR, not repaired: ja.wikipedia dates ep29 to 1983-05-05 while en.wikipedia and our stored row both say 1983-04-28 (there is a real preemption gap after ep27 on 1983-04-07). Two sources back the stored date, so I left it; noting it only so it is not rediscovered later.
